title: About SYNGAP1
content: SYNGAP1-related disorder is a rare genetic condition caused by a variant in the SYNGAP1 gene. It is associated with developmental delay, epilepsy, and autism spectrum features. CURE SYNGAP1 shares plain-language introductions for families who have just received a diagnosis.

title: Clinical trials and research
content: CURE SYNGAP1 tracks clinical trials and research studies relevant to SYNGAP1 families, including what taking part usually involves and how trials are listed. Families interested in a specific study are asked to speak with their own clinician and to follow the enrollment instructions published by the study sponsor.

title: Start a fundraiser
content: Supporters can run their own fundraiser for CURE SYNGAP1. The process is to pick an idea such as a birthday campaign, a walk, or a community event, set up a fundraising page, and share it with friends and family. The foundation provides logos, messaging, and a staff contact to help.

title: Donate
content: Donations to CURE SYNGAP1 fund research and clinical trial work for SYNGAP1-related disorder. One-time and recurring gifts are accepted online, and the foundation is a registered nonprofit, so gifts may be tax deductible.

title: Patient registry
content: CURE SYNGAP1 maintains a patient registry so that families can contribute data that helps researchers understand SYNGAP1-related disorder and plan studies. Joining involves creating an account and completing survey questions about the person's diagnosis and history.

title: Newly diagnosed families
content: Families who have just received a SYNGAP1 diagnosis can find a starting point here, including what the diagnosis means, questions worth asking a care team, and how to connect with other SYNGAP1 families.

title: Events and conference
content: CURE SYNGAP1 runs community events and a family conference where families, clinicians, and researchers meet. Event dates, locations, and registration details are published as each event is scheduled.

title: Contact CURE SYNGAP1
content: Families and supporters can reach the CURE SYNGAP1 team through the contact page for questions the website does not answer, including questions about fundraising, donations, and getting connected with other families.
